register: clear neutral Modern Standard Arabic for a personal finance application

digitAndBidiPolicy.generalRule: RTL Arabic interface with explicit bidirectional isolation for embedded LTR data
digitAndBidiPolicy.numericDisplayDecision: Arabic numeric display and separators must be implemented only with tested locale-aware formatters; parser compatibility and stored numeric values must not change
digitAndBidiPolicy.userAuthoredText: preserve byte-for-byte and isolate direction without translating or reshaping stored content

mandatoryQualityRules: Translate all 791 fixed source texts manually in product context before runtime activation.
Use natural Modern Standard Arabic; do not copy Persian, Urdu, Hebrew, Turkish, English or another integrated language into visible Arabic UI.
Implement all six Arabic cardinal plural categories and explicit dual forms for dynamic counts.
Avoid unnecessary gendered direct address; when gender is unavoidable, use neutral product wording rather than assuming the user’s gender.
Use Flutter RTL directionality and Arabic shaping; never reverse Arabic strings, amounts, dates, codes or user text manually.
Wrap embedded LTR values with safe bidirectional isolation so currency codes, IBAN, times, identifiers and Latin user text remain readable.
Preserve every user-authored name, note, bank name, title and custom message byte-for-byte.
Keep country, interface language and default currency independent, and never convert or merge currencies in reports.
Reports, charts, PDF, CSV, notifications and stored relationships must remain semantically identical to the selected-language screen.

Do not activate Arabic runtime until static copy, dynamic grammar, RTL, bidi isolation, language purity, storage, CSV, report, PDF, notification, responsive, visual, full regression and release artifact gates pass.
Protect all fourteen integrated languages and the accepted overdue-day and Android background-notification fixes.
Use neutral financial terminology and avoid legal, religious, political or region-specific claims not present in the source.
